western_tropical.label: Western Tropical

mother.notes: Primary nurturer; modern reading may reassign to whichever parent was more home-oriented.

father.notes: Authority/legacy figure; modern reading may reassign to the more dominant or boundary-setting parent.

siblings.notes: Includes cousins and the childhood peer/neighborhood environment.

children.notes: 5th house = first child. Subsequent children traditionally read from houses 5+2n (7th, 9th, ...).

spouse.notes: Descendant axis. Committed partnership, legal contracts, the 'other' in close relationship.

general_lineage.notes: Accumulated family wealth/values, inherited speech patterns, early upbringing tone.

western_tropical.notes: Sullivan's 'water houses' framework: 4th (roots), 8th (inherited trauma/resources), 12th (unconscious/hidden family material).

vedic.label: Vedic / Jyotish

father.notes: Some traditional systems use the 5th house instead of the 9th.

siblings.notes: 3rd house = younger siblings; 11th house = older siblings and extended social network.

general_lineage.notes: Family wealth, lineage, speech, and immediate upbringing.

vedic.notes: Same water-house logic applies, though some traditional Vedic schools weight the 9th (father/dharma/lineage) more heavily for ancestral material than the 8th.

planetary_thread_rules.description: Rules for detecting recurring planetary combinations ('threads') across family members, per Lynn Bell's genogram method.
planetary_thread_rules.notes: A thread is flagged when the same planet-pair + aspect-type combination (e.g., Moon-Pluto square) appears in 2 or more family members' natal charts, independent of house placement.
